newsitem.title: UK: Bradys up on short covering after tame U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: Bradys up on short covering after tame U.S. CPI.

text.p: Emerging debt prices rallied during the European afternoon amid short-covering following benign U.S. inflation data.

Dealers also reported outright buying after the U.S. consumer price index for March came in slightly lower than average forecasts, prompting a one-point upward spike in long-dated U.S. Treasury prices.
The CPI report allayed market fears of acceleration in price growth and was seen as easing the pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

With the U.S. long bond up around a point, Mexico's benchmark 30-year dollar bond MXUMS=RR had added 1.375 points to 103.875 bid by 1400 GMT. Argenine Brady bonds were up by 0.25-0.75 point while Russian minfin paper was quoted 0.25-0.50 point firmer.
Russian debt was also buoyed by the announcement it will launch a second dollar Eurobond, dealers said.
Russia announced plans for the deal through the office of First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais.
A statement quoting Chubais said the issue would have a maturity of at least five years and be lead managed by J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg.
Those two banks also lead managed Russia's debut Eurobond, a $1.0 billion offering last November which was heavily oversubscribed. -- Dan Lalor, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
